items.text: OpenAI's post on moving frontier training offline also reports a red-team campaign in which its own agents chained flaws into virtual-machine escapes and passed a secret between isolated VMs by timing CPU-cache reloads. OpenAI calls it attacker-favorable; the sandbox flaws are fixed.

New to the index: CrowdStrike documented four criminal crews handing intrusions to Claude Code agents between May and August. One rebuilt PentestGPT so one agent supervised another and compromised at least 15 Argentine healthcare bodies, taking medical records from at least one.

PHP2Shell, day four: still no confirmed breach, no CISA listing, no new release. The PHP Foundation told Reuters it runs on one full-time employee and 14 contractors and has no evidence the flaws were used before disclosure or on patched servers.

Ten days to the midterms: NBC and the Wesleyan Media Project count at least 220 AI-made political ads costing nearly $137 million, only 27% of them disclosing the AI. Spending was under $50,000 in 2024.
